title: Capstone: Build a Complete Personal Website
summary: Build one cumulative portfolio website that grows from one page into a complete semantic, accessible multi-page site.

sketchBlocks.title: Build one portfolio website, one milestone at a time
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
A local career-readiness mentor wants a polished personal portfolio website that can be reviewed before you begin learning CSS.

You are the **beginner web developer** responsible for the whole website.

This is **one cumulative project**, not a collection of separate exercises. The workspace will grow only when the project needs a new file:

1. Start with `index.html` only.
2. Add `about.html` when the About page is introduced.
3. Add `projects/portfolio.html` and `images/profile.png` when Projects and image paths are introduced.
4. Keep those same files while you add structured content and semantic markup.
5. Add `contact.html` only when you build the contact form.
6. Finish by reviewing and validating the complete site.

Once a file appears, it stays in every later milestone.

Every task gives you the **exact visible text, labels, link text, table values, and form wording** to use. You are practicing HTML structure and integration, not inventing portfolio copy.

Your final deliverable is one complete multi-page portfolio website that combines document structure, navigation, relative paths, an image asset, lists, a table, semantic markup, accessibility, and a form.

quizDraft.title: Step 1: Build the Home page
quizDraft.prompt:
Work only in `index.html`. Do not create any other files yet.

Replace the starter content with this exact visible text:

- Main heading: `Jordan Lee`
- First paragraph: `Aspiring web developer building practical projects for the community.`
- Second paragraph: `This portfolio introduces my background, projects, and contact information.`

Keep the page title exactly `Jordan Lee | Home`. Preview the page, then click Check Answer.
quizDraft.hint: Only `index.html` belongs in the project at this milestone.

help.concept: Start with one real Home page. The rest of the site will be introduced only when the project needs it.
help.hint_1: Use the exact two paragraph sentences from the task.
help.hint_2: Do not create About, Projects, Contact, or image files yet.

quizDraft.title: Step 2: Add the About page and first navigation
quizDraft.prompt:
Keep your completed Home page and add one new file: `about.html`.

In `index.html`, add navigation with exactly these links:

- `Home` → `index.html`
- `About` → `about.html`

Then add this exact sentence after the existing Home paragraphs:

`Read more on the About page.`

Make only the words `About page` link to `about.html`.

In `about.html`, use:

- Page title: `Jordan Lee | About`
- Main heading: `About Jordan`
- The same `Home` and `About` navigation
- First paragraph: `I am learning web development by building useful pages and reviewing how each HTML element communicates meaning.`
- Second paragraph: `My current goal is to build clear, accessible websites before moving on to CSS.`

Do not create Projects, Contact, or image files yet.
quizDraft.hint: This milestone introduces exactly one new page: About.

help.concept: The website is cumulative: keep Home and add About, then connect the two pages.
help.hint_1: Use the exact link text `Home` and `About`.
help.hint_2: Use the exact About paragraphs provided; do not invent biography text.

quizDraft.title: Step 3: Add Projects, relative paths, and the image
quizDraft.prompt:
Keep `index.html` and `about.html`. Add these two project items now:

- New page: `projects/portfolio.html`
- Image asset: `images/profile.png`

Update the navigation on Home and About to exactly:

- `Home`
- `About`
- `Projects`

On root pages, `Projects` must link to `projects/portfolio.html`.

In `index.html`, display `images/profile.png` with exact alt text:

`Portrait of Jordan Lee`

Then add this exact Home sentence:

`See what I am building on the Projects page.`

Make only `Projects page` link to `projects/portfolio.html`.

In `projects/portfolio.html`, use:

- Page title: `Jordan Lee | Projects`
- Main heading: `Projects`
- Navigation links:
  - `Home` → `../index.html`
  - `About` → `../about.html`
  - `Projects` → `portfolio.html`
- Image path: `../images/profile.png`
- Exact image alt text: `Portrait of Jordan Lee beside a portfolio project`
- Paragraph: `I use small community-focused projects to practice HTML structure and accessibility.`

Do not create `contact.html` yet.
quizDraft.hint: Projects and the image appear now because this milestone needs them.

help.concept: The nested Projects page must use `../` to reach root-level files and the image folder.
help.hint_1: Use exactly `../index.html`, `../about.html`, and `../images/profile.png` from the nested page.
help.hint_2: Do not add Contact yet; that page belongs to the form milestone.

quizDraft.title: Step 4: Add structured content and semantic structure
quizDraft.prompt:
Improve the same Home, About, and Projects pages. Do not add any new files in this milestone.

Use `header`, `nav`, `main`, and `footer` on all three pages.

On Home, add:

- Section heading: `Welcome`
- Exact sentence: `Explore my skills and project progress.`
- Link only `skills` to `about.html`
- Link only `project progress` to `projects/portfolio.html`
- Footer text: `Jordan Lee's HTML portfolio.`

On About, add these exact headings and list items:

- `My learning path`
- `Skills I'm practicing`
- `Semantic HTML structure`
- `Accessible forms and labels`
- `Multi-page navigation and relative paths`

Use this exact footer sentence:

`Return to the portfolio home page.`

Make only `portfolio home page` link to `index.html`.

On Projects, use an `article` and add:

- Heading: `What I'm building`
- Heading: `Project progress`

Create this exact table:

| Project | Focus | Status |
| Community Event Page | Semantic content | Complete |
| Workshop Signup | Accessible forms | Complete |

Then add this exact sentence:

`For HTML reference material, I use MDN Web Docs.`

Make only `MDN Web Docs` link to `https://developer.mozilla.org/`.

Use footer text:

`Jordan Lee's project portfolio.`
quizDraft.hint: No files are added here; this milestone improves the pages already in the project.

help.concept: Lists and tables should carry real portfolio information while semantic elements describe the page structure.
help.hint_1: Copy the exact three skills and the exact two table rows.
help.hint_2: Keep all navigation and image paths from the previous milestone.

quizDraft.title: Step 5: Add the Contact page and accessible form
quizDraft.prompt:
Keep every existing file and add one new file now: `contact.html`.

Add `Contact` to the navigation on every page.

Use these exact Contact paths:

- From Home and About: `contact.html`
- From Projects: `../contact.html`

In `index.html`, add this exact sentence:

`Have a project idea or learning opportunity? Send me a message.`

Make only `Send me a message` link to `contact.html`.

Build `contact.html` with:

- Page title: `Jordan Lee | Contact`
- Main heading: `Contact Jordan`
- Section heading: `Start a conversation`
- Paragraph: `Share a project idea or learning opportunity.`

Use this exact form content:

- Label: `Name` → text input
- Label: `Email address` → email input
- Group legend: `Reason for contacting me`
- Radio choice: `Project idea`
- Radio choice: `Learning opportunity`
- Label: `Message` → textarea with 5 rows
- Submit button: `Send message`

Use footer text:

`Jordan Lee's HTML portfolio.`
quizDraft.hint: Contact appears only now because this is the milestone where the form becomes part of the real website.

help.concept: Keep the existing site and extend its navigation to the new Contact page.
help.hint_1: Use matching `for` and `id` values for Name, Email address, and Message.
help.hint_2: Use a fieldset and legend for the two related reason choices.

quizDraft.title: Step 6: Review and validate the whole website
quizDraft.prompt:
Do not add any new files. Review the complete five-file website.

Add these exact meta descriptions:

- Home: `Personal portfolio of Jordan Lee, an aspiring web developer sharing skills, projects, and contact information.`
- About: `About Jordan Lee and the HTML skills currently being practiced.`
- Projects: `Portfolio projects by Jordan Lee demonstrating semantic HTML and accessibility.`
- Contact: `Contact Jordan Lee about project ideas and learning opportunities.`

On Projects, add `scope="col"` to the three table headers:

- `Project`
- `Focus`
- `Status`

On Contact, add `required` to:

- Name
- Email address
- Message

Then use Preview to navigate:

`Home → About → Projects → Contact`

From Projects, also test the links back to Home and About and confirm the image still loads from `../images/profile.png`.

Do not change the exact visible content from earlier milestones.
quizDraft.hint: This milestone verifies the finished site; it does not introduce another page or exercise.

help.concept: A final review checks metadata, relative paths, image loading, structured content, semantics, accessibility, and forms together.
help.hint_1: Use the exact four meta descriptions in the task.
help.hint_2: Navigate the actual site in Preview after the source checks pass.
